new_scholarship.name: IUJ Nakayama Premium Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The Nakayama Premium Scholarship is funded and awarded by the International University of Japan itself, as part of the scholarship scheme it operates for non-Japanese applicants. IUJ's official 'Tuition & Scholarships' page lists it in the table of scholarships applied for through IUJ with the conditions '100% tuition', 'Partial admissions fee' and 'JPY 100,000 monthly stipend', available to Master's and PhD students. It is decided competitively at the time of admission, and applicants request it inside the IUJ online application system rather than through a separate external application. Applications are currently open for IUJ's September 2027 entry.

new_scholarship.description: DGIST's international graduate admissions site publishes a Graduate Scholarship page describing two scholarship tracks for admitted international graduate students. The Government Scholarship track, described as scholarship benefits funded by the Korean government, provides full tuition coverage plus an annual stipend of at least KRW 9.6 million for Master's students and at least KRW 14.04 million for PhD students, with additional incentives varying by research performance, and is open to DGIST's science and engineering departments. DGIST states that admission to the graduate school guarantees automatic registration to the scholarship without any additional process, so the award follows admission rather than a separate scholarship application. The next published admission window is the 2027 Spring 3rd round, whose online application period runs 5-19 November 2026.

new_scholarship.description: The Global Learners Scholarship was established by HKUST to support the University's strategic objective of enhancing the diversity of its student community. Applicants do not apply for it: all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are considered automatically, and the decision is normally communicated with the offer of admission. Awardees receive a full tuition waiver that is renewable for the normal duration of the study, subject to satisfactory academic performance, and a School or Programme Office may add a top-up as long as the combined limit of full tuition fee plus an HK$60,000 annual allowance is not exceeded. The University opened its online application system for 2027/28 entry in early October 2026, with a Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026.

new_scholarship.description: The ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship is a fully funded grant run through Institut Teknologi Bandung's financial aid office for selected young applicants from partner countries in ASEAN, the Asia-Pacific and Africa who want to study at Indonesia's leading technological university. The published package covers the whole S1 degree: full exemption from tuition fees for all eight academic semesters, a monthly living allowance of IDR 4,700,000, a one-time arrival settlement of IDR 10,000,000 to secure private off-campus accommodation, a round-trip economy air ticket at cost to Jakarta, basic health insurance and visa fee coverage.
